import pandas as pd

# Read the source CSV file with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_49/training_0.csv", index_col=0)

# Since only one source table is given, no union or join with other tables is possible.
# The failed pipeline grouped by title and aggregated min(rank_on_list) and max(weeks_on_list),
# but the output had more rows than target (1170 vs 1162).
# This suggests some titles have trailing spaces or case differences causing duplicates.
# We apply string normalization on 'title' to unify them before grouping.

# Normalize 'title' by stripping whitespace and converting to uppercase (or lowercase)
source0['title'] = source0['title'].str.strip()

# Group by normalized title and aggregate min rank_on_list and max weeks_on_list
result = source0.groupby('title', as_index=False).agg(
    min_rank=('rank_on_list', 'min'),
    max_weeks_on_list=('weeks_on_list', 'max')
)

# Write the result to the target CSV file with exact column names
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_49/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
